title: API 510 Practice Questions 2026: 30 MCQs with Answers & Code References
snippet: 2026 API 510 exam prep: 30 practice MCQs with full explanations, ASME VIII Div 1 and API 510/571/572/580 references, exam tips, study plan and FAQ.
content:
This 2026 practice question bank prepares candidates for the API 510 Pressure Vessel Inspector certification exam administered by the American Petroleum Institute (API). The questions below are referenced to the API 510 Body of Knowledge (BOK), with primary code references to API 510 Pressure Vessel Inspection Code (In-service Inspection, Rating, Repair, and Alteration), API RP 572 (Inspection Practices for Pressure Vessels), API RP 576 (Inspection of Pressure-Relieving Devices), API RP 577 (Welding Inspection and Metallurgy), API RP 580 (Risk-Based Inspection), API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 (Fitness-for-Service), and ASME BPVC Sections V, VIII Div 1, and IX.

API 510 Exam Format Overview

The API 510 exam is administered as a computer-based test (CBT) at Prometric centers in two parts:

  • Closed-book: 50 multiple-choice questions in 2 hours and 45 minutes. Covers general knowledge of vessel inspection, basic metallurgy, NDT, welding, corrosion, and code requirements that can be answered without reference materials.
  • Open-book: 60 to 80 multiple-choice questions in 4 hours and 45 minutes. Candidates use the full set of API 510 reference publications (downloaded as searchable PDFs at the test center).
  • Pass mark: 70% (combined or per section depending on cycle).
  • Recertification: Every 3 years (with reduced exam) and 6 years (full exam).

API 510 Practice Questions

Question 1: Per API 510, the maximum interval between external inspections of a pressure vessel is:

  • A. 1 year
  • B. 3 years
  • C. 5 years
  • D. 10 years

Correct Answer: C

Explanation: Per API 510 Section 6.4, external inspection intervals shall not exceed 5 years or the required internal/on-stream inspection interval, whichever is less. Insulated vessels follow the same rule with CUI considerations.

Question 2: The maximum internal inspection interval for a pressure vessel is:

  • A. The lesser of half the remaining life or 10 years
  • B. 5 years
  • C. 20 years
  • D. Never required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 510 Section 6.5.1 limits the internal (or on-stream) inspection interval to the lesser of one-half the remaining corrosion life or 10 years. RBI-based intervals can extend this with proper justification under API 580.

Question 3: Long-term corrosion rate is calculated by:

  • A. Initial thickness minus current thickness divided by time since installation
  • B. Current thickness divided by years in service
  • C. Wall loss in the last year
  • D. Not calculated

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Long-term corrosion rate (LTCR) = (t-initial − t-actual) / (years between t-initial and t-actual). Short-term rate (STCR) uses the period between the previous and current inspection. The greater rate is generally used for remaining life calculations.

Question 4: Per API 510, a pressure vessel weld repair requires:

  • A. No special procedure
  • B. Written repair plan approved by the inspector and engineer, qualified WPS, qualified welders, NDT, and post-weld treatment as required
  • C. Only welder qualification
  • D. Only NDT after repair

Correct Answer: B

Explanation: API 510 Section 8 requires a documented repair plan, qualified WPS/PQR per ASME IX, qualified welder/welding operator, applicable NDT, and post-weld heat treatment (PWHT) where required by original construction code or alteration analysis.

Question 5: A vessel’s MAWP is governed by:

  • A. Hydrostatic test pressure
  • B. The weakest component, calculated using current thickness less FCA
  • C. Operator preference
  • D. Nameplate pressure regardless of corrosion

Correct Answer: B

Explanation: MAWP is the maximum pressure at which the weakest component will safely operate, calculated using current measured thickness minus the future corrosion allowance (FCA). MAWP is updated when corrosion or alterations change the rating.

Question 6: Per API 580, RBI (Risk-Based Inspection) uses:

  • A. Probability of failure (PoF) × Consequence of failure (CoF) = Risk
  • B. Only corrosion rate
  • C. Only vessel age
  • D. Random selection

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Risk = PoF × CoF. PoF accounts for damage mechanisms, inspection effectiveness, and remaining life; CoF accounts for safety, environmental, and business impact. The risk matrix drives inspection planning per API 580/581.

Question 7: Pressure relief valve (PRV) inspection per API 510 and API 576 must occur:

  • A. At the same interval as the vessel internal inspection, not to exceed 5 years (clean service) or 10 years for RBI
  • B. Every 20 years
  • C. Never
  • D. Only when leaking

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 510 Section 6.6 and API 576 typically require PRV testing/inspection every 5 years (clean services) or 10 years (RBI-justified). PRVs in severe or fouling service may require more frequent inspection.

Question 8: Per ASME VIII Div 1 Appendix 3, the minimum thickness for a cylindrical shell under internal pressure is:

  • A. t = PR / (SE − 0.6P)
  • B. t = PD / 2S
  • C. t = PR / (SE + 0.4P)
  • D. Determined by test only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASME VIII Div 1 UG-27: t = PR / (SE − 0.6P) for circumferential stress (governs thin-walled cylinders). The alternate formula t = PR / (2SE + 0.4P) for longitudinal stress is rarely governing. Joint efficiency E depends on RT.

Question 9: An on-stream inspection differs from internal inspection in that:

  • A. It is performed while the vessel is in service using NDT from outside
  • B. It requires shutdown
  • C. It is illegal
  • D. Only used for tanks

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: On-stream inspection uses external NDT (UT, RT, profile RT, guided wave UT, PEC) to assess vessel condition without entry. Per API 510, on-stream may substitute for internal inspection if the inspector and engineer can determine vessel integrity to the same degree.

Question 10: Per API 510, an authorized pressure vessel inspector must:

  • A. Hold a current API 510 certification and the experience requirements of API 510 Section 4
  • B. Hold ASNT Level III in all methods
  • C. Be a licensed PE
  • D. Be the vessel owner

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Authorized inspectors must hold current API 510 certification with required experience (4-year degree + 1 yr, or 2-year degree + 2 yrs, or HS + 3 yrs, etc.) and operate under a quality system. PE is required only when API 510 specifies engineer involvement.

Question 11: When a vessel has a corrosion rate of 0.1 mm/yr, FCA of 1.6 mm, current thickness of 12 mm, minimum required thickness of 10 mm, the remaining life is:

  • A. 4 years
  • B. 20 years
  • C. 100 years
  • D. 2 years

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Remaining life = (t-actual − t-min) / corrosion rate = (12 − 10) / 0.1 = 20 years (without FCA) or (12 − 10 − 1.6) / 0.1 = 4 years if FCA must be retained. API 510 uses the more conservative number for inspection planning.

Question 12: Per API 510 alteration vs repair definition, an alteration is:

  • A. Any physical change that changes the design conditions, vessel rating, or geometry
  • B. Any weld repair
  • C. Replacement of a gasket
  • D. External painting

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Per API 510, an alteration changes the design conditions (T, P, MAWP), vessel rating, or geometry (e.g., adding a nozzle). A repair restores the vessel to a condition suitable for safe operation without changing the rating. Alterations require engineering review.

Question 13: Hot tapping refers to:

  • A. Welding on equipment in service while contents are flowing
  • B. Cleaning the vessel with steam
  • C. Heat treatment
  • D. Hydrostatic test

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Hot tapping is welding (typically a nozzle) onto a pressurized line or vessel and then drilling through. API RP 2201 governs hot tap procedures including burn-through prevention, hazard analysis, and procedure qualification.

Question 14: Per API 510, weld overlay used as a repair must:

  • A. Be classified as a temporary repair only
  • B. Use a qualified WPS, NDT after welding, and PWHT if required
  • C. Not be permitted
  • D. Use bolted patches

Correct Answer: B

Explanation: Weld overlay (build-up) repairs are permitted as permanent repairs under API 510 Section 8, requiring qualified WPS, qualified welders, NDT, and PWHT if mandated by base metal P-number or carbon equivalent rules.

Question 15: A fillet weld patch (lap patch) is:

  • A. A permanent repair
  • B. A temporary repair limited by API 510 Section 8.1.5
  • C. Always prohibited
  • D. A nozzle attachment

Correct Answer: B

Explanation: Fillet welded patches are permitted as temporary repairs per API 510 Section 8.1.5 with limits on size, design analysis, NDT, and a defined service period until a permanent repair can be made.

Question 16: Per ASME VIII Div 1 UCS-79, post-weld heat treatment is required when:

  • A. Always
  • B. Based on P-number, thickness, and service per UCS-56 tables
  • C. Only stainless
  • D. Never required

Correct Answer: B

Explanation: ASME VIII Div 1 UCS-56 specifies PWHT requirements based on material P-number and nominal thickness. Common rule: P-No. 1 carbon steel typically needs PWHT above 19 mm (3/4 in) thickness; lower-alloy steels at lesser thickness.

Question 17: API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 Level 1 assessment is for:

  • A. Conservative screening calculations using look-up tables and simple formulas
  • B. Finite element analysis only
  • C. Material replacement
  • D. Never used

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 579 organizes Fitness-for-Service assessments in three levels: Level 1 (conservative tables/formulas), Level 2 (more detailed calculations with material properties), Level 3 (advanced FEA / probabilistic). The inspector typically performs Level 1; engineers Level 2 and 3.

Question 18: Stress corrosion cracking (SCC) in stainless steel is typically caused by:

  • A. Chloride ion exposure at elevated temperature
  • B. Carbon dioxide
  • C. Sulfur
  • D. Inert gas

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Chloride stress corrosion cracking (Cl-SCC) of austenitic stainless steel (304/316) occurs typically above 60°C in chloride-bearing solutions. Insulation chlorides leaching with water is a common source. API RP 581 lists SCC mechanisms.

Question 19: Per API RP 577, hydrogen damage in welds includes:

  • A. Hydrogen-induced cracking (HIC), sulfide stress cracking (SSC), HTHA
  • B. Only fatigue
  • C. Only creep
  • D. Only erosion

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API RP 577 and API 571 cover hydrogen damage: HIC (blistering and crack networks in wet H2S), SSC (sulfide stress cracking in hard welds and HAZ), HSC (hydrogen stress cracking), and HTHA (high-temperature hydrogen attack — Nelson curves).

Question 20: Per API 510, a vessel that has had a major repair must be:

  • A. Hydro-tested at 1.3 × MAWP or otherwise verified
  • B. Hydrotested at MAWP only
  • C. Vented
  • D. Replaced

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Hydrostatic test pressure after major repair/alteration is typically 1.3 × MAWP × (Sa/Sd) per ASME VIII Div 1 UG-99, where Sa/Sd is the stress ratio at test/design temperatures. Alternative NDT and engineering analysis may substitute.

Question 21: The most common NDT method for verifying vessel wall thickness from outside is:

  • A. Ultrasonic thickness gauging (UT)
  • B. Liquid penetrant
  • C. Magnetic particle
  • D. Visual only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: UT thickness is the workhorse NDT for vessel wall measurement. Spot UT at TML (thickness measurement locations) and scanning UT (corrosion mapping) are both used. Profile RT, PAUT corrosion mapping, and PEC for through-insulation are also acceptable.

Question 22: A vessel’s thickness measurement location (TML) is selected based on:

  • A. Damage mechanism, geometry (heads, shells, nozzles), and historical thinning
  • B. Random
  • C. Only the manway
  • D. Anywhere convenient

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: TMLs are placed at expected damage locations based on the dominant damage mechanism, geometry (shells, heads, knuckle radii, nozzles, manways), inlet/outlet, level lines, and historical thinning. API RP 572 provides guidance on TML selection.

Question 23: Per API 510, the inspector’s authority includes:

  • A. Approving repair plans, accepting NDT results, and verifying conformance to code
  • B. Designing new vessels
  • C. Setting operating pressure
  • D. Hiring welders without qualification

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The authorized inspector is responsible for verifying inspection, repair, and alteration activities meet API 510 and applicable code. Design and reratings involve the engineer (PE or qualified equivalent).

Question 24: Joint efficiency E in ASME VIII Div 1 depends on:

  • A. Type of joint and extent of radiography
  • B. Only the welder
  • C. Pressure
  • D. Material density

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASME VIII Div 1 Table UW-12 gives joint efficiencies based on joint type (Type 1 butt weld, Type 2 single-V, etc.) and radiography category (Full, Spot, None). Typical values: E=1.0 for Type 1 with full RT; E=0.85 with spot; E=0.70 with no RT.

Question 25: A nameplate on a pressure vessel must include:

  • A. Manufacturer, MAWP, design temperature, year built, serial number, code stamp
  • B. Only serial number
  • C. Only manufacturer
  • D. No requirement

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASME VIII Div 1 UG-119 requires the nameplate to include manufacturer, MAWP, design temperature, MDMT, year of construction, manufacturer’s serial number, and the appropriate ASME code stamp (U, UM, etc.).

Question 26: Per API 571, sulfidation corrosion typically occurs:

  • A. At elevated temperatures in sulfur-containing hydrocarbon streams (e.g., crude unit, FCC)
  • B. At ambient temperature
  • C. Only in stainless
  • D. Only with water

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Sulfidation is high-temperature corrosion of iron-based alloys by sulfur compounds, typically above 260°C. The McConomy curves and modified McConomy provide thinning rate vs. temperature, sulfur content, and material. Common in crude distillation and FCC units.

Question 27: A pressure vessel under cyclic service may be subject to:

  • A. Fatigue damage
  • B. Only creep
  • C. No damage
  • D. Only corrosion

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Pressure cycles, thermal cycles, and vibration can initiate and propagate fatigue cracks, particularly at stress concentrations (nozzles, weld toes). API RP 579-1 Part 14 provides fatigue assessment procedures.

Question 28: The minimum design metal temperature (MDMT) of a vessel is:

  • A. The lowest metal temperature at which the vessel can safely contain pressure
  • B. Ambient temperature
  • C. Operating temperature
  • D. Hydrotest temperature

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: MDMT is the lowest expected metal temperature considering operation, startup, shutdown, and upsets. Material toughness must be sufficient at MDMT per UCS-66 charts. Brittle fracture risk increases as temperature drops below MDMT.

Question 29: Per API 510, a temporary repair must be replaced with a permanent repair:

  • A. By the next scheduled turnaround, or as specified in the repair plan
  • B. Never — temporary repairs are permanent
  • C. Within 1 hour
  • D. Only if leaking

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Temporary repairs are limited in scope and time. API 510 Section 8.1.5 requires them to be replaced with a permanent repair by the next scheduled turnaround or as documented in the engineering and inspector-approved repair plan.

Question 30: Welder qualification per ASME IX requires:

  • A. Successful welder performance qualification (WPQ) test record
  • B. Only a written test
  • C. Visual inspection only
  • D. No qualification needed

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASME IX requires a welder performance qualification (WPQ) including production of a test coupon and acceptable NDT (RT or bend testing). The WPQ has essential variables that, if changed, may require requalification. Welders must maintain continuity (typically welding within the 6 months prior).

Study Tips for API 510

  • Master the BOK: Download the API 510 Body of Knowledge from the API Individual Certification Programs (ICP) page. Every question on the exam maps to a BOK item.
  • Use the right edition: The exam references specific editions of API 510, RP 572, RP 576, RP 577, RP 580, ASME V, VIII Div 1, IX, and API 571. Check the API ICP body of knowledge document for the current exam cycle.
  • Tab your books: Open-book is open-book in name only — if you cannot find the answer in 90 seconds, you will not finish. Tab key sections in every reference: API 510 Sections 5-8, ASME VIII UG-22 to UG-37 and UG-99, ASME IX QW-200 to QW-300.
  • Practice calculations: MAWP from t-min, remaining life, corrosion rates, joint efficiency, hydrotest pressure. Plan on 200+ calculation problems before the exam.
  • Read API 571: Damage mechanisms appear on every exam. Memorize the 30+ mechanisms in API 571 with morphology and typical NDT.

Recommended Study Materials

  • API 510 Pressure Vessel Inspection Code (current edition)
  • API RP 572 Inspection Practices for Pressure Vessels
  • API RP 576 Inspection of Pressure-Relieving Devices
  • API RP 577 Welding Inspection and Metallurgy
  • API RP 580 Risk-Based Inspection
  • API 571 Damage Mechanisms Affecting Fixed Equipment
  • ASME BPVC Sections V, VIII Div 1, and IX
  • Atlantis NDT API 510 exam preparation course

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What experience do I need to sit the API 510 exam?

A: API 510 requires combinations like: BS in engineering plus 1 year, or 2-year engineering degree plus 2 years, or high school plus 3 years of NDT/inspection-related experience. Verify the current API ICP requirements.

Q: How long does API 510 certification last?

A: 3 years to a reduced recertification exam (open-book only), then 6 years for the full recertification exam. Continuous practice as an inspector is also required.

Q: Are API 510 and ASNT certifications the same?

A: No. API 510 certifies you as a vessel inspector (a code-driven role); ASNT certifies you in NDT methods (UT, RT, MT, PT, etc.). Many inspectors hold both. See our ASNT vs PCN comparison for NDT body certifications and our ASNT certification page for ASNT routes.

Q: Is API 510 recognized internationally?

A: Yes. API 510 is widely recognized globally, especially in oil & gas. In Europe, PED-driven Notified Body assessments may also apply. In Saudi Aramco SAES requirements explicitly reference API 510 inspectors.

Q: What is the difference between API 510 and API 570?

A: API 510 covers pressure vessels; API 570 covers in-service piping. See our API 510 vs API 570 comparison.

Q: Does Atlantis NDT offer API 510 review courses?

A: No. Atlantis NDT does not run API 510 exam-preparation courses. Our API 510 pressure vessel inspection support is ASNT Level III technical work on vessel programmes — RBI, FFS and data review — not exam coaching.

Q: Can I take the API 510 exam online?

A: API exams are administered through Prometric test centers worldwide (computer-based test). Online proctoring options have been piloted; verify the latest with API ICP at the time of registration.

Q: What is the API 510 exam pass rate?

A: Industry averages range from 50 to 65% first attempt. Candidates from structured prep courses typically report 80%+ first try.

Q: How much does an API 510 certified inspector earn?

A: In the US, $90,000 to $140,000/year base, plus offshore/turnaround premiums. In the Middle East, $7,000 to a modest cost/month tax-free for experienced inspectors. Salary scales with API 570 + 653 stacking.

Q: Does the API 510 exam include ASME IX?

A: Yes — welding procedure and welder performance qualification under ASME IX is a major open-book topic. Tab QW-200 (WPS/PQR), QW-300 (welder performance), and QW-400 (essential variables tables).

About Atlantis NDT

Atlantis NDT is a global NDT technology and services company headquartered in Houston, Texas with operations across India and the Middle East. We deliver accredited NDT training, technical consulting, certification preparation, and digital inspection software trusted by oil & gas, fabrication, EPC, and power generation clients. Our team of ASNT Level III instructors has trained thousands of inspectors worldwide.

Whether you are preparing for ASNT certification, API 510, API 570, or API 653, our exam preparation programs combine classroom theory, hands-on practical training, and proctored mock exams that mirror the real test environment.

Call us at +1 (281) 840-8969 or email sales@atlantisndt.com to enroll in the next training cohort. Same-day quotes for corporate group training in Houston, Dubai, Riyadh, Hyderabad, and on-site at your facility.

title: API 570 Practice Questions 2026: 30 Piping Inspector MCQs & Answers
snippet: 2026 API 570 piping inspector practice exam: 30 multiple-choice questions, code references (ASME B31.3, API 570/571/574/577), study tips and FAQ.
content:
This 2026 practice exam bank prepares candidates for the API 570 Piping Inspector certification. The questions reflect the API 570 Body of Knowledge (BOK) and reference API 570 Piping Inspection Code (In-service Inspection, Rating, Repair, and Alteration), API RP 574 (Inspection Practices for Piping System Components), API RP 577 (Welding Inspection and Metallurgy), API RP 578 (Material Verification Program), API RP 580 (Risk-Based Inspection), API 571 (Damage Mechanisms), ASME B31.3 (Process Piping), and ASME B16.5, BPVC V and IX.

API 570 Exam Format Overview

  • Closed-book: ~50 questions on basic principles, NDT, welding, corrosion, code requirements that should be remembered.
  • Open-book: ~80 questions referencing the full API 570 publications package.
  • Total time: 7.5 hours (closed + open).
  • Pass mark: 70%.
  • Recertification: 3-year reduced and 6-year full cycle.

API 570 Practice Questions

Question 1: Per API 570, the maximum interval for visual external inspection of Class 1 piping is:

  • A. 5 years
  • B. 10 years
  • C. 1 year
  • D. Never

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 570 Table 6.1 gives Class 1 piping maximum external inspection interval of 5 years (or 1/2 remaining life). Class 2 is 5 years, Class 3 is 10 years, Class 4 is optional. Class definitions depend on consequence (toxic/flammable/etc.).

Question 2: Class 1 piping per API 570 is:

  • A. Highest consequence (e.g., flammable services that vaporize, anhydrous HF, H2S above 3%)
  • B. Lowest consequence
  • C. Tanks
  • D. Vessels only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 570 classifies piping by consequence: Class 1 highest (flashing flammables, HF, H2S above 3%, anhydrous HCl), Class 2 (most flammables, on-site steam, acids/caustics), Class 3 (flammables that do not vaporize, non-toxic), Class 4 (water, plant air).

Question 3: Per ASME B31.3, the minimum required thickness of straight pipe under internal pressure is:

  • A. t = PD / (2(SE + PY))
  • B. t = PR / 2S
  • C. t = D / 10
  • D. Determined experimentally

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASME B31.3 Eq. 3a: t = PD / (2(SE + PY)) where P = pressure, D = OD, S = allowable stress, E = quality factor, Y = coefficient from Table 304.1.1. Add mill tolerance (typically 12.5%) and corrosion allowance for required nominal thickness.

Question 4: A thickness measurement location (TML) for piping is typically:

  • A. At elbows, tees, reducers, and high-velocity/turbulent zones where erosion/corrosion is expected
  • B. Anywhere convenient
  • C. Only on straight runs
  • D. Never on fittings

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Per API 570 and RP 574, TMLs concentrate at locations of expected damage: elbows (extrados & intrados), tees, reducers, dead legs, injection points, mixing points, vents/drains, and at known damage mechanism locations.

Question 5: Injection points per API 570 require:

  • A. Special inspection circuits with dedicated TMLs upstream, downstream, and at the injection point
  • B. No special inspection
  • C. Removal at every turnaround
  • D. Visual only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Injection points (e.g., corrosion inhibitor, water, antifoulant injection) experience accelerated localized corrosion downstream. API 570 Section 6.2.2.5 requires dedicated inspection circuits with TMLs from 12 in upstream to 25 ft (or 3 pipe diameters) downstream.

Question 6: Corrosion under insulation (CUI) is most likely on piping in service between:

  • A. −12 to 175°C (10 to 350°F), with peak risk near dew point
  • B. Above 500°C only
  • C. Cryogenic only
  • D. Not real

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: CUI is most aggressive in the temperature range where moisture can be present beneath the insulation: −12 to 175°C (carbon steel). API 570 and API RP 583 give CUI risk-based inspection guidance. Stainless can suffer chloride SCC in this same range.

Question 7: Dead legs in piping are concerning because:

  • A. Stagnant fluid concentrates corrosion attack
  • B. They reduce pressure drop
  • C. They are required by code
  • D. They prevent corrosion

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Dead legs (block valves, vent lines, dead-end caps) accumulate stagnant fluid, water, sediment, or vapor that drive localized corrosion, MIC, and freeze damage. API 570 requires identification and special inspection of dead legs.

Question 8: Per API 570, online (on-stream) inspection may be used in lieu of internal inspection when:

  • A. External NDT can determine the integrity of the piping with equivalent confidence
  • B. The owner waives the inspection
  • C. Pressure is below 50 psi
  • D. Never

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Most piping cannot be entered for internal inspection. API 570 requires external NDT (UT, RT, guided wave UT, PEC, PAUT corrosion mapping) at intervals that establish integrity. Internal inspection at openings is performed where access allows.

Question 9: A piping system suffering high temperature hydrogen attack (HTHA) per API 941 (Nelson curves) typically has:

  • A. Service above hydrogen partial pressure / temperature limits for the alloy
  • B. Service in air only
  • C. Cold service
  • D. Vacuum service

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: HTHA per API 941 occurs in carbon and low-alloy steels exposed to hydrogen partial pressure and elevated temperature combinations that exceed Nelson curve limits. AUBT (Advanced Ultrasonic Backscatter Technique), TOFD, and metallographic replication are used to detect HTHA.

Question 10: Per API RP 578, a material verification program (PMI) is required to:

  • A. Verify alloy components are the specified material grade
  • B. Measure thickness
  • C. Detect cracks
  • D. Test welds only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Positive Material Identification (PMI) uses portable XRF or OES to verify alloy composition during construction, repair, and in-service. API RP 578 prevents catastrophic failures from material mix-ups (e.g., carbon steel instead of 5Cr-1/2Mo in a hot piping system).

Question 11: Per API 570, the maximum thickness measurement interval for Class 1 piping is:

  • A. 5 years or 1/2 remaining life, whichever is less
  • B. 10 years
  • C. 20 years
  • D. Never required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 570 Table 6.1 limits Class 1 thickness measurement to 5 years (or 1/2 remaining life). Class 2 also 5 years, Class 3 is 10 years, Class 4 optional. RBI may modify these intervals.

Question 12: An authorized piping inspector per API 570 must:

  • A. Hold current API 570 certification and meet experience requirements
  • B. Hold ASNT Level III
  • C. Be a PE
  • D. Be the owner

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 570 Section 4 requires the inspector to hold current API 570 certification, experience per the API ICP requirements, and operate under the owner/user’s inspection management system.

Question 13: A repair to in-service piping per API 570 requires:

  • A. Written repair plan approved by inspector and engineer, qualified WPS, qualified welders, NDT, and post-weld treatment as required
  • B. Just the welder’s name
  • C. Only the engineer
  • D. No documentation

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 570 Section 8 requires documented repair plans, qualified WPS/PQR per ASME IX or B31.3 Chapter V, qualified welders, applicable NDT, and PWHT as required by base metal and service.

Question 14: A bolted clamp on a leaking pipe is:

  • A. A temporary repair allowed under specific API 570 limits
  • B. Always prohibited
  • C. A permanent solution
  • D. Required at every flange

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Bolted clamps and enclosures (e.g., engineered leak repair) are temporary repairs that must be designed, documented, and replaced with a permanent repair by the next planned turnaround per API 570 Section 8.

Question 15: ASME B31.3 sets the allowable stress S based on:

  • A. The lower of UTS/3, YS/1.5, creep, or rupture data at temperature
  • B. Only UTS
  • C. Only YS
  • D. Manufacturer choice

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASME B31.3 Table A-1 allowable stress S is the lowest of (UTS at T)/3, (UTS at 38°C)/3, (YS at T)/1.5, (YS at 38°C)/1.5, and creep/rupture rules. Different ratios apply for high-pressure piping (Chapter IX).

Question 16: A flange rating per ASME B16.5 (e.g., Class 150, 300, 600) refers to:

  • A. Pressure-temperature rating tables for various materials
  • B. Outside diameter
  • C. Bolt count
  • D. Manufacturer code

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: B16.5 Class is a pressure rating that varies with material group and temperature. For example, Class 300 carbon steel (Group 1.1) rates 740 psig at 100°F and drops to 290 psig at 850°F. Each class has a full temperature-pressure curve.

Question 17: A test pressure for piping per ASME B31.3 is typically:

  • A. 1.5 × design pressure (hydrostatic) or 1.1 × (pneumatic)
  • B. 1.0 × design
  • C. 5 × design
  • D. No test required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: B31.3 paragraph 345 specifies hydrostatic test at 1.5 × design pressure adjusted for temperature ratio, or pneumatic at 1.1 × design with hazard considerations. Sensitive leak testing is allowed under specific conditions.

Question 18: Per API 571, naphthenic acid corrosion (NAC) typically affects:

  • A. Crude unit vacuum tower and side draws at 220 to 400°C, high TAN crudes
  • B. Sour water piping
  • C. Refrigerated services
  • D. Steam lines

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: NAC affects crude distillation and vacuum unit piping when TAN exceeds 0.5 mg KOH/g, in the 220 to 400°C window, with high velocity/turbulence. 316/317 stainless or 5Cr-1/2Mo with selective upgrade are typical remedies.

Question 19: A pipe support that is missing or damaged may cause:

  • A. Excessive thermal stress, sag, fatigue, and accelerated wear at adjacent supports
  • B. No issue
  • C. Improved flow
  • D. Heat loss only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Inspectors should record damaged or missing pipe supports during external inspection. Loss of support shifts loads to remaining supports, creates fatigue, and may cause excessive stress in nozzles and flanges.

Question 20: Per API 570, soil-to-air interface inspection on buried piping is critical because:

  • A. Accelerated corrosion occurs at the transition due to moisture, coatings damage, and aeration
  • B. Decoration
  • C. Maintenance access only
  • D. Not required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The soil-to-air interface (typically 6 in below grade to 12 in above) experiences accelerated external corrosion. API 570 Section 9.2.1 requires inspection of these zones including coating removal where indicated.

Question 21: A piping system with intermittent service that allows water accumulation may suffer:

  • A. Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC)
  • B. No damage
  • C. Only creep
  • D. Only fatigue

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: MIC by sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) and other microbes accelerates pitting and weld metal corrosion. Common in firewater piping, intermittent service lines, and hydrotest water left in pipe. API 571 documents MIC mechanisms and inspection.

Question 22: A guided wave UT (GWUT) survey on piping is best for:

  • A. Screening long lengths of pipe for significant cross-section reductions
  • B. Crack sizing
  • C. Surface flaw detection
  • D. Hardness

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: GWUT sends low-frequency (20 to 100 kHz) torsional/longitudinal waves along the pipe wall. It detects cross-sectional area changes (typically >5%) up to 30 to 50 m on insulated, buried, or elevated pipe. It is a screening tool, not a sizing tool.

Question 23: Pulsed eddy current (PEC) inspection of insulated piping detects:

  • A. Average wall thickness loss through insulation without removal
  • B. Surface cracks
  • C. Painted welds
  • D. Internal liquid

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: PEC pulses a magnetic field through insulation/weather jacket and measures the decay to estimate average wall thickness. It is a screening tool for CUI — not absolute thickness. Spot UT after PEC indications is standard practice.

Question 24: A piping circuit per API 570 is:

  • A. A grouping of piping with similar service, material, and damage potential for inspection planning
  • B. Only one pipe
  • C. Tank only
  • D. Vessels

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Piping is grouped into inspection circuits by service, material, expected damage mechanism, and operating conditions. Each circuit has a defined set of TMLs and inspection records. API RP 574 provides circuit definition guidance.

Question 25: Per ASME B31.3, branch reinforcement is required when:

  • A. The header is weakened by the branch opening beyond the limits in para 304.3
  • B. Always
  • C. Only for vacuum
  • D. Never

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASME B31.3 paragraph 304.3 requires branch reinforcement calculation. If header thickness in excess of pressure-design accounts for the removed material, no extra reinforcement is needed; otherwise, pads, weldolets, or wall thickness must compensate.

Question 26: A flange leak path most commonly occurs at:

  • A. The gasket seating surface due to inadequate bolt torque, gasket damage, or thermal cycling
  • B. The pipe wall
  • C. The nut threads
  • D. Never

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Most flange leaks are gasket seating issues. Proper bolt torque (per ASME PCC-1), gasket selection (compatible with service), and avoiding flange face damage are key. Hot-bolting (re-tightening at operating temperature) is sometimes needed.

Question 27: A pipe wall thickness reading of 9.5 mm on a 10.0 mm nominal pipe with 12.5% mill tolerance is:

  • A. Acceptable within mill tolerance (minimum 8.75 mm)
  • B. Unacceptable
  • C. Indicates massive corrosion
  • D. Always rejected

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Mill tolerance on seamless pipe is 12.5% under nominal. A 10 mm nominal pipe could be as thin as 8.75 mm new. 9.5 mm is normal new-pipe variation; corrosion is not implied unless previous baseline was higher.

Question 28: Per API 570 owner/user responsibilities include:

  • A. Establishing the inspection program, classifying piping, supervising the inspector
  • B. Performing the inspection personally
  • C. Designing the piping
  • D. Only welding

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 570 places the program responsibility with the owner/user, who classifies piping, sets inspection intervals, employs authorized inspectors and engineers, and maintains records. The inspector verifies code compliance.

Question 29: A piping system below MDMT during a startup may be at risk of:

  • A. Brittle fracture
  • B. Creep
  • C. Sulfidation
  • D. Erosion

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Carbon steel below MDMT (often around −29°C for non-impact-tested A106) loses toughness and may fail brittlely when pressurized. Cold blowdowns and autorefrigeration upsets must be analyzed and limited.

Question 30: NDT methods commonly used by an API 570 inspector include:

  • A. VT, UT thickness, UT shear wave, RT (profile), PT, MT, PAUT, GWUT, PEC, MFL
  • B. Only VT
  • C. Only RT
  • D. Hardness

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: An API 570 inspector commands a broad NDT toolbox: visual, thickness UT, shear wave UT (for cracks), profile RT, PT, MT, PAUT, TOFD, GWUT, PEC, MFL, eddy current array. The inspector selects techniques based on the damage mechanism — not the other way around.

Study Tips for API 570

  • Master ASME B31.3: Especially para 304 (design), Chapter V (fabrication and inspection), and the allowable stress tables in Appendix A. B31.3 is heavily referenced on open-book questions.
  • Know the damage mechanisms: API 571 is essential. Memorize CUI, MIC, NAC, sulfidation, HTHA, chloride SCC, caustic embrittlement, and their typical NDT.
  • Practice TML and remaining life calculations: Long-term and short-term corrosion rates, remaining life with and without FCA, MAWP for a piping circuit.
  • Tab your code books: API 570 sections 5 to 9, ASME B31.3 para 304/Chapter V/Appendix A, ASME IX QW-200 essential variables, API RP 574 inspection methods.
  • Practice 300+ MCQs: Work through several hundred practice questions across all eight reference codes before exam day.

Recommended Study Materials

  • API 570 Piping Inspection Code (current edition)
  • API RP 574 Inspection Practices for Piping System Components
  • API RP 577 Welding Inspection and Metallurgy
  • API RP 578 Material Verification Program
  • API RP 580 Risk-Based Inspection
  • API 571 Damage Mechanisms
  • ASME B31.3 Process Piping
  • ASME BPVC Sections V and IX
  • Atlantis NDT API 570 exam preparation course

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is the difference between API 570 and API 510?

A: API 570 covers in-service piping inspection; API 510 covers in-service pressure vessels. See our API 510 vs 570 comparison.

Q: Can I take API 570 before API 510?

A: Yes — the API ICP certifications are independent. Many inspectors take API 510 first (more vessel work) but API 570 first is fine.

Q: How long does API 570 certification last?

A: 3 years to the reduced recertification, 6 years to the full exam recertification.

Q: What is API 570 Class 1 piping?

A: The highest consequence category — toxic, flammable that vaporizes on release, HF acid, H2S above 3%. Class 1 has the shortest inspection intervals.

Q: Is hot tapping covered in API 570?

A: API 570 references API RP 2201 for hot tapping procedures. Pre-tap NDT, qualified hot tap WPS, and burn-through prevention are required.

Q: Does Atlantis NDT offer corporate group API 570 training?

A: No. Atlantis NDT does not run API 570 exam-preparation courses. Our API 570 piping inspection support is ASNT Level III technical work on piping programmes, not exam coaching.

Q: Is API 570 recognized in the Middle East and India?

A: Yes — widely recognized by Aramco, ADNOC, KOC, QatarEnergy, Reliance, Indian Oil, BPCL, and most major refineries.

Q: What is the API 570 exam pass rate?

A: Industry averages 50 to 65% first try. Structured prep typically lifts this to 80%+.

Q: How much does an API 570 inspector earn?

A: US base $90,000 to $135,000/year; Middle East a modest cost to a modest cost/month tax-free. Adding API 510 + 653 stacks significantly (a 510+570+653 inspector commonly earns $150,000+ in the US).

Q: How does API 570 relate to CSWIP 3.1?

A: CSWIP 3.1 is a welding inspection certification commonly used in welding fabrication QC. API 570 is in-service piping inspection. Many inspectors hold both for complete fabrication-to-service coverage.

About Atlantis NDT

Atlantis NDT is a global NDT technology and services company headquartered in Houston, Texas with operations across India and the Middle East. We deliver accredited NDT training, technical consulting, certification preparation, and digital inspection software trusted by oil & gas, fabrication, EPC, and power generation clients. Our team of ASNT Level III instructors has trained thousands of inspectors worldwide.

Whether you are preparing for ASNT certification, API 510, API 570, or API 653, our exam preparation programs combine classroom theory, hands-on practical training, and proctored mock exams that mirror the real test environment.

title: API 653 Practice Questions 2026: 30 Tank Inspector MCQs with Answers
snippet: 2026 API 653 tank inspector exam prep: 30 practice MCQs with explanations, API 653/650/575/651 references, settlement analysis, NDT, and study tips.
content:
This 2026 question bank prepares candidates for the API 653 Aboveground Storage Tank (AST) Inspector certification. Questions reference API 653 Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction, API 650 Welded Tanks for Oil Storage, API RP 575 Inspection Practices for AST, API RP 577 Welding, API 571 Damage Mechanisms, API RP 651 Cathodic Protection, API RP 652 Linings for Tank Bottoms, and ASME BPVC V and IX.

API 653 Exam Format Overview

  • Closed-book: ~50 questions on basic principles, welding, NDT, corrosion, tank components.
  • Open-book: ~80 questions referencing the API 653 publication package.
  • Total time: 7.5 hours.
  • Pass mark: 70%.
  • Recertification: 3-year reduced, 6-year full cycle.

API 653 Practice Questions

Question 1: Per API 653, the maximum interval between external inspections of an AST is:

  • A. 5 years
  • B. 10 years (or RBI-determined, not to exceed 20)
  • C. 1 year
  • D. Never required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 6.3.2.1 requires external inspection at least every 5 years or RBI-determined intervals up to a maximum that depends on shell-thickness measurement intervals and remaining life calculations.

Question 2: The maximum interval for internal inspection of an AST (out-of-service) is:

  • A. 10 years if no corrosion rate is known; otherwise based on bottom remaining life
  • B. 5 years always
  • C. 30 years
  • D. Never required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 6.4 limits the internal inspection interval based on bottom corrosion rate and remaining life: not to exceed 20 years; first internal inspection within 10 years for tanks without known corrosion rate; can be extended with RBI per Section 6.4.2.2 to a maximum of 30 years.

Question 3: A typical tank bottom is most susceptible to corrosion:

  • A. Underside from the soil due to moisture and pH
  • B. Top only
  • C. Never
  • D. Only at welds

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The product side and the underside both corrode, but underside (soil-side) corrosion is often the limiting factor for tank life. API RP 651 (cathodic protection) and API RP 652 (internal linings) are commonly applied to extend bottom life.

Question 4: Per API 653, the minimum thickness for the bottom plate is calculated based on:

  • A. Remaining life, corrosion rate, and protection method
  • B. Tank height only
  • C. Diameter only
  • D. Owner preference

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 4.4 sets minimum bottom plate thickness based on calculated corrosion rate, projected service interval, and whether the underside has release prevention barrier (RPB), cathodic protection, or lining. Common values 2.5 to 5 mm depending on protection.

Question 5: Tank settlement evaluation per API 653 Annex B compares:

  • A. Measured settlement to allowable uniform, planar tilt, and out-of-plane settlement
  • B. Tank diameter to height
  • C. Wind load to tank weight
  • D. Not evaluated

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Annex B provides methods to evaluate settlement: uniform (no shell distress), planar tilt (allowable based on H/D), edge settlement (between shell and bottom), out-of-plane (Fourier analysis to evaluate bending stresses).

Question 6: Per API 653 Section 4.3, the minimum thickness of the shell course is calculated by:

  • A. 1-foot method or variable design point method using current measured thickness less FCA
  • B. ASME VIII formula
  • C. Material specification only
  • D. Owner choice

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 uses the same 1-foot method (Eq. 4-1) and variable-design-point method (Section 4.3.3.2) as API 650 for required shell thickness, applied with measured thickness less FCA to determine fitness for continued service.

Question 7: A floating roof has potential damage from:

  • A. Seal wear, pontoon leaks, corrosion under sediment, drain hose failure, ice loading
  • B. Only the seal
  • C. No damage possible
  • D. Only welds

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Floating roof external inspection per API 653 includes seals (primary, secondary), pontoon compartments (must be inspected internally), deck plates, drain hoses, anti-rotation devices, and emergency overflow drains. Pontoon flooding causes catastrophic sinking events.

Question 8: Per API 653 Section 9, a major alteration to a tank requires:

  • A. Engineering review, qualified WPS, NDT, and possibly hydrostatic test
  • B. Only welder qualification
  • C. No documentation
  • D. Owner decision only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: A major alteration (e.g., shell height change, new nozzles in stressed areas, foundation rework) requires engineering review per API 653 Section 9, qualified procedures and welders per ASME IX, NDT per API 650 acceptance criteria, and hydrotest per Section 12.

Question 9: A magnetic flux leakage (MFL) floor scanner is used to:

  • A. Detect bottom plate corrosion and pitting on internal inspection
  • B. Measure shell thickness
  • C. Detect cracks
  • D. Verify alloy

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: MFL scanners cover large areas of tank floor rapidly during internal inspection, detecting product-side and underside metal loss. Suspect areas are then confirmed with UT prove-up. API 653 references quantitative thresholds (e.g., 20% wall loss).

Question 10: Per API 653, hydrostatic test pressure for a tank after reconstruction is:

  • A. Full liquid head to maximum design liquid level
  • B. 1.5 × design
  • C. No test
  • D. Pneumatic only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASTs are tested by filling with water to the maximum operating liquid level (or the design liquid level for new tanks). API 650 paragraph 7.3.6 provides hydrotest procedures. There is no pressure multiplier; full-head water test demonstrates the static-only loading.

Question 11: An authorized API 653 inspector must:

  • A. Hold current API 653 certification with required experience
  • B. Be the owner
  • C. Hold a PE license
  • D. Be a welder

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 4 requires current certification under the API ICP program with experience as listed (e.g., BS + 1 yr, AS + 2 yr, HS + 3 yr in NDT/inspection of fixed equipment).

Question 12: An overlay weld repair on a tank bottom is permitted when:

  • A. Per API 653 Section 7 with qualified WPS, NDT, and within thickness/area limits
  • B. Never
  • C. Always
  • D. Only by replacement

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Bottom plate repairs include patch plates (lap-welded or butt-welded), overlay (build-up), or full plate replacement. API 653 Section 9 specifies size limits, weld details, and NDT (typically vacuum box testing on bottom welds).

Question 13: A vacuum box test on a tank bottom weld is performed at:

  • A. 0.21 to 0.55 bar (3 to 8 psi) below atmospheric, with soap solution applied to weld
  • B. 1.5 bar above atmospheric
  • C. No vacuum
  • D. 10 bar

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 650 Section 7.3.4 specifies the vacuum box method: apply soap solution, place box over weld, draw partial vacuum (typically 3 to 8 psi). Bubble formation indicates a through-weld leak. Standard for tank bottom welds.

Question 14: Per API 653, a temporary repair is:

  • A. Limited in scope and time, to be replaced with a permanent repair within a defined period
  • B. Permanent
  • C. Not allowed
  • D. Always required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Temporary repairs (e.g., clamps, doublers) are allowed under API 653 with engineering review and a documented timeline for permanent repair, typically by the next turnaround.

Question 15: Per API RP 651, cathodic protection of tank bottoms uses:

  • A. Galvanic (sacrificial) anodes or impressed current
  • B. Paint only
  • C. Concrete
  • D. No protection

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Underside CP uses either sacrificial anodes (typically Mg or Zn) for small tanks or impressed current systems for larger tanks. Effectiveness measured at −850 mV (Cu/CuSO4 reference) per NACE SP0169 and API RP 651.

Question 16: Per API 653, the minimum interval for ultrasonic thickness measurement of the shell is:

  • A. Calculated from corrosion rate; not to exceed 15 years for tanks without RBI
  • B. Annually
  • C. Once at construction
  • D. 30 years

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 6.3.3 sets external UT thickness intervals based on corrosion rates: 5 years (uncoated above-grade), 10 years (known low corrosion), 15 years (lined or CP-protected internally), with RBI extensions. External UT can be done while tank is in service.

Question 17: An edge settlement (between bottom and shell) is critical because:

  • A. Bending stresses can cause shell-to-bottom weld cracks
  • B. Only cosmetic
  • C. Improves drainage
  • D. No concern

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Edge settlement (sometimes called dish-out) creates bending of the bottom plates near the shell, generating high secondary stresses at the chime weld. API 653 Annex B provides evaluation criteria based on length and depth.

Question 18: A roof rafter inspection during internal entry must check:

  • A. Section thickness loss, rafter clip attachment, top angle, deck plate corrosion
  • B. Only the column
  • C. Only welds
  • D. Not required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Fixed cone/dome roof internals: rafters, columns (lateral movement and base plates), top angle, deck plates (corrosion from acidic vapor space), and overflow/vent screens. RP 575 details fixed roof inspection.

Question 19: Per API 653, an API 650 nameplate must be attached to:

  • A. The tank, in a permanent and accessible location
  • B. The piping
  • C. The roof
  • D. Never required

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Per API 650 Section 10, the nameplate identifies manufacturer, year built, design code edition, capacity, maximum operating liquid level, design metal temperature, specific gravity, and the API monogram. Original nameplates must be preserved on reconstruction.

Question 20: A tank that has been out of service for an extended period requires:

  • A. Verification of inspection records, condition assessment, and potential re-inspection before returning to service
  • B. No action
  • C. Always full reconstruction
  • D. Pneumatic test only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Idle tanks may suffer from internal humidity corrosion, settlement, foundation issues, biological growth. API 653 requires a re-commissioning condition assessment per Section 6 prior to return to service.

Question 21: Per API 653, a release prevention barrier (RPB) is:

  • A. A secondary containment beneath the tank bottom to detect leaks
  • B. A dike
  • C. A vent
  • D. A roof

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: RPB systems (e.g., HDPE liner, concrete pad with leak detection grooves) detect underside leaks and prevent soil/groundwater contamination. EPA SPCC and many state regulations require RPB for new and reconstructed tanks.

Question 22: A linear out-of-roundness on a tank shell can indicate:

  • A. Foundation settlement or wind damage
  • B. Improved capacity
  • C. No concern
  • D. Painted surface

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Tank shell roundness is measured externally with optical or laser methods. Out-of-roundness beyond API 653 limits indicates uneven foundation settlement, wind buckling, vacuum collapse, or installation defects requiring engineering review.

Question 23: Per API 571, atmospheric corrosion of an AST shell is accelerated by:

  • A. Industrial atmosphere, coastal salt, wet/dry cycles, broken paint
  • B. Dry desert
  • C. Vacuum
  • D. Inert gas

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: External atmospheric corrosion accelerates in industrial atmospheres (SO2, NOx), coastal (chlorides), wet/dry cycles, and where paint has failed. Recoating intervals depend on environment severity. API RP 652 covers lining; API 575 covers coating inspection.

Question 24: A tank nozzle stiffening per API 650 is required when:

  • A. The nozzle opening reduces shell pressure-bearing capacity below limits
  • B. Always
  • C. Never
  • D. Owner choice

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Nozzle reinforcement is calculated per API 650 Section 5.7.5 using area replacement rules. Reinforcement plates compensate for removed shell material. Low-type and regular-type nozzle details have prescribed reinforcement.

Question 25: Per API 653 Section 12, hydrostatic testing after major repair is required when:

  • A. The repair affects pressure-containing welds beyond limits specified in Section 12
  • B. Always
  • C. Never
  • D. Owner choice

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 12 specifies when hydrotest is mandatory after repair/alteration. Generally, replacement of significant shell plate areas, raising tank height, or modifying nozzles in critical zones requires hydrotest. Vacuum box testing is acceptable for bottom-only repairs.

Question 26: A tank double bottom installation is:

  • A. A repair where a new bottom is placed above the existing leaking bottom with annulus monitoring
  • B. New tank
  • C. Not allowed
  • D. Same as RPB

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Double bottom retrofit places a new bottom above the existing bottom with a small annular space (often filled with sand or instrumented for leak detection). This reduces downtime vs full bottom replacement. Engineering review for height/structural impact required.

Question 27: Per API 653, NDT methods commonly used on tanks include:

  • A. VT, UT thickness, MFL floor scan, PT/MT on welds, vacuum box, RT on shell welds
  • B. Only VT
  • C. Only hardness
  • D. Eddy current only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Tank inspection NDT: VT (mandatory), UT thickness on shell/roof, MFL on floor, PT/MT on critical welds, vacuum box on bottom and annular welds, RT on shell butt welds. PEC for through-coating screening. Settlement survey by total station/laser.

Question 28: Per API 653, a tank weld defect repair requires:

  • A. Excavation to sound metal, NDT to confirm, qualified WPS, post-repair NDT per acceptance criteria
  • B. Cover with paint
  • C. Replacement of full plate
  • D. No repair

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Standard weld repair sequence per ASME IX and API 650/653: excavate defect (grinding or arc gouging), NDT to confirm full removal (typically MT or PT), weld per qualified WPS, post-repair NDT (VT plus MT/PT/RT/UT as specified).

Question 29: Per API 653, the minimum thickness for tank annular ring plate is:

  • A. Calculated based on shell stress, with minimum values per Section 4.5
  • B. 1 mm always
  • C. 50 mm
  • D. No minimum

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Annular plates (the ring of thicker bottom plates beneath the shell) carry high stress from shell. API 653 Section 4.5 sets minimum thickness based on shell stress (S ≤ 23,200 psi gives 6 mm minimum; higher stress requires thicker annular). Stress-relieved welds may be required.

Question 30: A tank inspection report per API 653 must include:

  • A. Findings, calculations, NDT records, photos, repair recommendations, signed by authorized inspector
  • B. Verbal summary only
  • C. Photos only
  • D. Welder names only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: API 653 Section 13 requires comprehensive inspection records: tank ID and history, measured thicknesses, settlement data, NDT records, deficiencies and recommendations, calculations, photos, and the certified inspector’s signature.

Study Tips for API 653

  • Master settlement analysis: API 653 Annex B is heavily tested. Practice uniform, planar tilt, edge, and out-of-plane settlement evaluation by hand.
  • Tank components vocabulary: Annular ring, sketch plate, chime, knuckle, top angle, wind girder, rafter clip. Misidentifying components is a common exam pitfall.
  • Calculations: Shell thickness by 1-foot method, bottom remaining life, MAOL (maximum allowable operating liquid level), nozzle reinforcement.
  • Damage mechanisms: Underside soil corrosion, MIC, atmospheric, settlement-induced cracking. API 571 sections relevant to tanks.
  • Tab your books: API 653 Sections 4 to 13, API 650 Sections 5 (design) and 7 (fabrication), RP 575, RP 651, RP 652, RP 577.

Recommended Study Materials

  • API 653 Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction
  • API 650 Welded Tanks for Oil Storage
  • API RP 575 Inspection Practices for AST
  • API RP 651 Cathodic Protection of AST
  • API RP 652 Linings for AST Bottoms
  • API RP 577 Welding Inspection and Metallurgy
  • API 571 Damage Mechanisms
  • ASME BPVC V and IX
  • Atlantis NDT API 653 exam preparation course

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What experience is required for API 653?

A: BS + 1 year, AS + 2 years, HS + 3 years of NDT/inspection-related experience on fixed equipment. Verify current API ICP requirements.

Q: What is the difference between API 510, 570, and 653?

A: 510 = pressure vessels, 570 = piping, 653 = aboveground storage tanks. Stacking all three is common for refinery and terminal inspectors.

Q: Is API 653 valid for all tank types?

A: API 653 applies to API 650 / API 12 series welded storage tanks. Riveted tanks and bolted tanks have specific provisions; underground tanks are not in scope (governed by other codes).

Q: How often must a tank be inspected internally?

A: First internal inspection within 10 years if no corrosion data; thereafter based on bottom remaining life; up to 30 years with RBI per API 653 Section 6.4.2.2.

Q: What is a tank API monogram?

A: An API licensee monogram (API 650, 12F, 12D, etc.) certifies the tank was built to the applicable API standard by a licensed shop. Reconstruction work may also be monogrammed.

Q: Does Atlantis NDT offer API 653 review courses?

A: No. Atlantis NDT does not run API 653 exam-preparation courses. Our API 653 tank inspection support is ASNT Level III technical work on tank programmes, not exam coaching.

Q: How does floating roof inspection differ from cone roof?

A: Floating roofs add seals, pontoons, drain hoses, anti-rotation, ladder/stairway, and roof drainage. Cone/dome roofs add rafters, columns, and vent design. Both inspected under API 653 Section 6 and RP 575.

Q: What is the API 653 exam pass rate?

A: Industry first-attempt 50 to 60%; structured prep typically lifts this to 80%+.

Q: Is settlement always rejectable?

A: No — uniform settlement is usually benign. Differential settlement (tilt, edge, out-of-plane) must be evaluated per API 653 Annex B against allowable limits. Engineering review for borderline cases.

Q: How does API 653 relate to ASME B31.3 or API 510/570?

A: API 653 is for storage tanks. ASME B31.3 covers process piping. API 510 covers pressure vessels (over 15 psig). API 570 covers in-service piping. A terminal/refinery inspector typically holds all four.

About Atlantis NDT

Atlantis NDT is a global NDT technology and services company headquartered in Houston, Texas with operations across India and the Middle East. We deliver accredited NDT training, technical consulting, certification preparation, and digital inspection software trusted by oil & gas, fabrication, EPC, and power generation clients. Our team of ASNT Level III instructors has trained thousands of inspectors worldwide.

Whether you are preparing for ASNT certification, API 510, API 570, or API 653, our exam preparation programs combine classroom theory, hands-on practical training, and proctored mock exams that mirror the real test environment.

Call us at +1 (281) 840-8969 or email sales@atlantisndt.com to enroll in the next training cohort. Same-day quotes for corporate group training in Houston, Dubai, Riyadh, Hyderabad, and on-site at your facility.

title: ASNT Level 3 Basic Exam Prep 2026: Format, 25 Practice MCQs, Tips
snippet: Complete 2026 guide to the ASNT Level III Basic exam: format, scope, 25 practice MCQs across all five subject areas, study plan, recommended materials, FAQ.
content:
The ASNT NDT Level III Basic Examination is the foundational exam that every Level III candidate must pass before sitting the method-specific exams. This 2026 guide explains the exam format, scope, and gives 25 practice questions across all five subject areas. References to ASNT CP-189, SNT-TC-1A, ASNT NDT Handbook, applicable ASTM/ISO standards, and the ASNT Body of Knowledge.

ASNT Level III Basic Exam Format Overview

The Basic Exam is a closed-book 135-question, 3-hour computer-based test at a Prometric center. The five subject areas (each ~27 questions) are:

  • Personnel qualification & certification documents: SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ANSI/ASNT CP-105, ISO 9712
  • NDT methods other than the applicant’s primary methods: a working knowledge of all common NDT methods (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, LT)
  • Materials, fabrication, and product technology: Metallurgy basics, welding, casting, forging, machining, heat treatment
  • NDT applications and capabilities: What method to use for what defect/material
  • Pass mark: 70% on the combined exam

Once Basic is passed (valid for 5 years), candidates can sit the method exams: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, LT, and emerging methods (PAUT, AE, IR/T, NR).

ASNT Level III Basic Practice Questions

Question 1: SNT-TC-1A is published by:

  • A. ASNT
  • B. ASTM
  • C. ISO
  • D. API

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The American Society for Nondestructive Testing publishes SNT-TC-1A (Recommended Practice for Personnel Qualification and Certification in NDT) as a Recommended Practice, not a standard. Employers use it to develop their Written Practice.

Question 2: ASNT CP-189 differs from SNT-TC-1A in that:

  • A. CP-189 is a standard (mandatory when invoked); SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice
  • B. They are identical
  • C. CP-189 is older
  • D. SNT-TC-1A covers Level III only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: CP-189 ANSI/ASNT Standard for Qualification and Certification of NDT Personnel is a mandatory standard when contractually invoked. SNT-TC-1A is recommended practice; the employer adapts it via a Written Practice.

Question 3: Per SNT-TC-1A, a Level III may:

  • A. Develop, qualify, and approve procedures; train and certify Level I, II, III personnel; interpret codes
  • B. Only perform inspections
  • C. Only train Level I
  • D. Only sign reports

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The Level III responsibilities per SNT-TC-1A para 5.3 are broad: develop procedures, approve them, qualify and certify Level I/II/III, interpret codes and specifications, perform NDT, designate NDT methods and techniques.

Question 4: Per SNT-TC-1A, the maximum interval between vision examinations is:

  • A. 12 months
  • B. 5 years
  • C. 10 years
  • D. Once at certification

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: SNT-TC-1A para 8.2 requires annual near vision (Jaeger J1 or equivalent at 12 in / 30 cm) and triennial color vision exam. CP-189 has similar requirements.

Question 5: Which NDT method is best suited for detecting subsurface laminations in plate steel?

  • A. Ultrasonic testing (UT)
  • B. Liquid penetrant (PT)
  • C. Magnetic particle (MT)
  • D. Visual

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Subsurface laminations parallel to the rolled plate surface are detected by straight beam UT (loss of backwall echo and intermediate echoes). MT and PT can only detect surface-breaking flaws.

Question 6: Eddy current testing (ET) is most useful for:

  • A. Conductive material surface and near-surface flaws, coating thickness, sorting alloys
  • B. Subsurface in non-conductive material
  • C. Concrete
  • D. Wood

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ET works on electrically conductive materials. It detects surface and near-surface cracks (limited by skin depth, typically 1 to 5 mm), measures conductivity (alloy sorting), and measures non-conductive coating thickness over conductive substrate.

Question 7: Carbon steel has a typical Curie point of:

  • A. 770°C
  • B. 100°C
  • C. 1500°C
  • D. 50°C

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Above the Curie temperature (~770°C for iron), the material becomes paramagnetic. Below it is ferromagnetic. MT cannot be performed above the Curie point.

Question 8: Which welding process is most prone to hydrogen-induced cracking (HIC) if not properly controlled?

  • A. SMAW (stick) with damp electrodes
  • B. TIG (GTAW)
  • C. Brazing
  • D. Friction stir welding

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: SMAW with low-hydrogen electrodes that have absorbed moisture (or non-low-hydrogen electrodes) introduces hydrogen into the weld. HIC develops in the HAZ of hardenable steels. Electrode storage and baking is critical.

Question 9: A cast steel part may have which characteristic defect?

  • A. Shrinkage cavities, gas porosity, hot tears, cold shuts, inclusions
  • B. Only fatigue
  • C. Only stress corrosion
  • D. No defects possible

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Casting defects (per ASTM E446, E186, E280) include shrinkage (centerline, dendritic), porosity (gas), hot tears (high-temperature cracking), cold shuts (failure of two metal streams to fuse), and inclusions. RT is the primary NDT for castings.

Question 10: A forged steel part typically has:

  • A. Refined grain structure with flow lines, fewer defects than castings
  • B. Always cracked
  • C. Identical to castings
  • D. No grain structure

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Forging plastically deforms the material, refining grain structure and aligning flow lines along the principal stress direction. Forged parts have higher fatigue and toughness than castings of the same alloy. Typical defects: laps, seams, internal bursts.

Question 11: ASTM E94 is a standard guide for:

  • A. Radiographic examination
  • B. Ultrasonic
  • C. Magnetic particle
  • D. Penetrant

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ASTM E94 (now superseded by parts of E1742, E1815, E2033, E2698) is the standard guide for radiographic examination. ASNT Level III candidates must know which ASTM standard governs each method.

Question 12: ISO 9712 is the international standard for:

  • A. NDT personnel qualification and certification
  • B. Welding consumables
  • C. Pressure vessels
  • D. Tank inspection

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 is the international NDT personnel qualification and certification standard, providing third-party certification (PCN, COFREND, etc.). It differs from SNT-TC-1A (employer-based US scheme).

Question 13: Charpy V-notch impact testing measures:

  • A. Notch toughness and ductile-to-brittle transition
  • B. Hardness only
  • C. Tensile strength only
  • D. Density

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Charpy testing strikes a notched specimen with a swinging pendulum at controlled temperatures, measuring energy absorbed. Used to determine ductile-to-brittle transition temperature and minimum design metal temperature.

Question 14: Quenching and tempering (Q&T) of steel produces:

  • A. High hardness/strength tempered to acceptable toughness
  • B. Maximum ductility only
  • C. Annealed structure
  • D. No change

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Quenching from austenitizing temperature forms hard martensite. Tempering at intermediate temperatures (typically 400 to 700°C) reduces brittleness while retaining significant strength. Common for pressure equipment, fasteners, gears.

Question 15: Acoustic emission (AE) testing detects:

  • A. Energy released during active material processes (crack growth, leak, deformation)
  • B. Static thickness
  • C. Surface roughness
  • D. Color

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: AE is a passive method: sensors detect transient elastic waves from active discontinuities (growing cracks, leaking joints, plastic deformation, corrosion product cracking). Used for tank floor leak testing, pressure vessel testing, bridge monitoring.

Question 16: Per SNT-TC-1A, training requirements for direct entry Level II:

  • A. Sum of Level I + Level II training and experience required
  • B. Only Level II training
  • C. No requirements
  • D. Level III approval only

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: SNT-TC-1A para 6.4 allows direct entry to Level II if the candidate satisfies the cumulative training and experience for Level I + Level II. The Written Practice must specifically permit this.

Question 17: Radiation safety units of equivalent dose are:

  • A. Sievert (Sv) and rem (1 Sv = 100 rem)
  • B. Gray and rad
  • C. Becquerel
  • D. Roentgen

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Equivalent dose accounts for radiation type and biological effect. SI unit Sievert, traditional rem. Absorbed dose units: Gray (SI), rad (traditional). Activity units: Becquerel (SI), Curie (traditional). Exposure: Coulomb/kg or Roentgen.

Question 18: A martensitic stainless steel (e.g., 410, 420) is:

  • A. Ferromagnetic and hardenable by heat treatment
  • B. Non-magnetic
  • C. Always soft
  • D. Cannot be welded

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Martensitic stainless (400 series) is ferromagnetic and can be hardened by Q&T. MT and PT both usable. Austenitic (300 series) is non-magnetic, not hardenable by heat treatment, but work-hardenable.

Question 19: Per SNT-TC-1A, a Level II inspector may:

  • A. Set up and calibrate equipment, perform inspections, interpret results, train Level I
  • B. Approve procedures
  • C. Certify Level III
  • D. Develop new methods

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Per para 5.2, Level II personnel are qualified to set up and calibrate equipment, perform tests per established procedures, interpret and evaluate, organize and report results, and provide on-the-job training to Level I personnel.

Question 20: The phenomenon of resonance in UT is used in:

  • A. Thin-wall thickness measurement
  • B. Subsurface defect detection
  • C. Surface roughness
  • D. Hardness

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Resonance occurs when a continuous wave is reflected back in phase between the front and back surfaces. Half-wavelength multiples of thickness produce resonance. Used historically for thin-wall thickness; now mostly replaced by pulse-echo digital gauges.

Question 21: A typical austenitic stainless steel grade is:

  • A. 304 or 316
  • B. 410
  • C. 4140
  • D. 6061

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: 304 (18Cr-8Ni) and 316 (18Cr-10Ni-2Mo) are common austenitic stainless steels. 410/420 are martensitic. 4140 is low-alloy carbon steel. 6061 is aluminum alloy.

Question 22: Welding heat-affected zone (HAZ) typically has:

  • A. Altered microstructure and properties due to thermal cycle
  • B. Same as base metal
  • C. Same as weld metal
  • D. No properties

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: The HAZ experiences temperatures from ambient (at the unaffected base metal boundary) up to the melting point (at the fusion line), creating microstructural gradients: grain growth, recrystallization, partial transformation. Often the most defect-prone region.

Question 23: Per CP-189, training records must be retained for:

  • A. Period specified by the employer’s quality system, typically the employee’s career plus several years
  • B. Until the employee leaves
  • C. No retention required
  • D. 1 year

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Personnel qualification records (training, experience, exams, vision, hands-on demonstration) must be retained per the employer’s documented quality system. Many industries (aerospace, nuclear) specify decades of retention.

Question 24: ISO 9712 certification is administered by:

  • A. Independent certification bodies (e.g., BINDT/PCN, COFREND, DGZfP)
  • B. The employer
  • C. The trainee
  • D. ASTM

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: ISO 9712 is a third-party certification model: the certification body is independent of both the employer and the candidate. PCN, COFREND, DGZfP, and ACCP are well-known schemes. Compare with our ASNT vs PCN article.

Question 25: A Level III may be qualified by:

  • A. ASNT third-party Level III exam (ACCP/Level III) or employer-administered exam under SNT-TC-1A
  • B. Self-declaration
  • C. Years of experience alone
  • D. Single training course

Correct Answer: A

Explanation: Most US Level IIIs hold the ASNT Level III certificate (Basic + Method exam, third-party administered). Under SNT-TC-1A, employers may also certify Level III, but most customers and codes (ASME, API) require ASNT Level III certificate.

Study Tips for the ASNT Level III Basic Exam

  • Cover all five subject areas evenly: Don’t over-focus on your primary method — you must score well across all five areas.
  • SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 paragraph by paragraph: Many candidates miss easy points on personnel qualification basics. Memorize paragraph numbers.
  • Learn cross-method knowledge: Even if you are a UT Level II, you must answer RT, MT, PT, ET, VT, LT questions confidently.
  • Materials science: Basic metallurgy, welding, casting, forging, heat treatment. The ASNT Level III Study Guide covers this well.
  • NDT applications: Know what method suits what defect/material. Practice scenario questions.

Recommended Study Materials

  • ASNT Level III Study Guide: Basic Examination
  • ASNT Recommended Practice SNT-TC-1A
  • ANSI/ASNT CP-189 Standard
  • ASNT NDT Handbook Volume 10 (Overview)
  • ISO 9712:2021 standard
  • ASTM Standards (E94, E709, E165, E1444, etc.)
  • Atlantis NDT Level III Basic exam preparation course

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How many questions on the ASNT Level III Basic exam?

A: 135 multiple-choice questions, 3 hours, closed-book, computer-based at Prometric.

Q: What is the pass mark for the Basic exam?

A: 70% overall. Some employers require higher composite scores combining Basic and Method exams.

Q: How long is the Basic exam valid?

A: 5 years. The candidate must pass at least one Method exam within this period to obtain Level III status. The Basic remains valid as long as at least one Method certificate is active.

Q: Can I take the Method exam without passing the Basic first?

A: No. Basic must be passed before the corresponding Method exam.

Q: How many ASNT Level III methods can I hold?

A: Unlimited — many Level IIIs hold UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, and ET. Each method requires its own Method exam after the Basic.

Q: Is ASNT Level III the same as PCN Level 3?

A: They are equivalent in industry recognition but follow different schemes. ASNT is employer-based or ACCP third-party (US); PCN is third-party (UK/global). See our ASNT vs PCN comparison.

Q: Does Atlantis NDT prepare candidates for the ASNT Level III Basic?

A: Yes — our 5-day Level III Basic prep course includes 500+ practice questions across all five subject areas, code/standard reference workshop, and a mock exam. Cohorts in Houston, Dubai, and on-site. Call +1 (281) 840-8969 to enroll.

Q: What is the typical Level III pass rate?

A: First-attempt pass rate for the Basic averages 50 to 65%. Atlantis prep students average 80%+.

Q: How much does a Level III earn?

A: US Level III $110,000 to $180,000+/year base; Middle East a modest cost to a modest cost/month tax-free. Multiple-method Level IIIs (UT, RT, MT, PT) command top of range. See L2 vs L3 article.

Q: Are there continuing education requirements for Level III?

A: ASNT does not mandate CEUs for renewal, but recertification at year 5 (and 10) requires re-examination unless the candidate accumulates points under the Recertification Through Points option.

About Atlantis NDT

Atlantis NDT is a global NDT technology and services company headquartered in Houston, Texas with operations across India and the Middle East. We deliver accredited NDT training, technical consulting, certification preparation, and digital inspection software trusted by oil & gas, fabrication, EPC, and power generation clients. Our team of ASNT Level III instructors has trained thousands of inspectors worldwide.

Whether you are preparing for ASNT certification, API 510, API 570, or API 653, our exam preparation programs combine classroom theory, hands-on practical training, and proctored mock exams that mirror the real test environment.

Call us at +1 (281) 840-8969 or email sales@atlantisndt.com to enroll in the next training cohort. Same-day quotes for corporate group training in Houston, Dubai, Riyadh, Hyderabad, and on-site at your facility.
